figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic illustration of the dual role of the GNW landscape in the dynamics of the cloud function Ψ. A minimum of the GNW landscape is represented by the potential well AΩ(x) (blue), whose effective depth is proportional to the attention degree A, and is associated with the recognition process, which drives the cloud function Ψ toward the minima of Ω(x). Information broadcasting across the GNW is associated with the potential barrier −icΩ(x) (red), which counteracts the localization of Ψ. A maximum of the GNW landscape is modeled by reversing the sign of the landscape, Ω(x) → −Ω(x), whereby the potential −AΩ(x) promotes the delocalization of Ψ, even though icΩ(x) formally becomes a potential well.
Figure 2: The phase diagram in the (U, g) parameter plane for the ground-state eigenfunctionΨ0(η). The curves Re E0 = 0 and Re µ = 0 originate at g = 1/ √ 3 and g = 1, respectively.
Figure 3: Illustration of the cloud-function dynamics corresponding to the supraliminal attended processing regime.
Figure 4: Illustration of the stepwide emergence of stimulus representations in the GNW when the attention degree A exceeds the threshold Ac.
Figure 5: Illustration of the cloud-function dynamics near a maximum of the GNW landscape, modeled by the potential (7) with the sign of its amplitude reversed, U → −U.
